_why: Prompt text as data (spec/08, task T3). tools/prompt.mjs assembles the document a human pastes into Claude Design from this file plus rules/contract-rules.json, so the prompt and the validator cannot drift. Reasoning prose stays in spec/08; this file is the normative text.
_topics_how: A topic is one statement the prompt makes about a subject, shared by every target that declares it. Each target lists its topics and states each one verbatim in claims, so two selected targets claiming a topic either agree word for word or the assembly is refused instead of concatenated: a subject can never appear twice in the document with two different answers. A claim that is not one of the block's own lines is a data error, because the statement would then hide from the cross-check. Engine-specific lines (which layout system this target has) deliberately carry no topic: they are scoped to the target's own heading and are allowed to differ, which is the point of a target block.
targetAwareness: Target awareness: this design will be converted to {targets} by a tool, not read by a human designer. The TARGET RULES below are not preferences, they are capability limits: a design that needs a capability a target lacks must be redesigned, not annotated. Where several targets are named, the design has to work on all of them, so a capability only one target has is a capability this design may not use.
sharedHeading: TARGET RULES shared by every target named above. They are listed once, not once per target.

targets.label: Compose / Compose Multiplatform

claims.clipping: Corner clipping does not come free: if a rounded container holds a child with its own background, say which shape the child must use.
claims.elevation: Elevation is a declared step, data-elevation with one of 0, 1, 3, 6, 8 or 12, and never a drawn box-shadow.
claims.fonts: Text size is a user setting, so a layout that only works at one text size is a bug: check every row where text can grow.
claims.grid: A grid is a decision and not a layout feature: wherever this design shows a two-dimensional layout, declare its minimum cell width with data-grid-min.
claims.icons: Icons are named whatever draws them: put data-icon="ic_name" on every icon and prefer inline SVG with fill="currentColor", because a glyph font can be named but never converted.
claims.safe-area: Safe area insets are a runtime value. Never bake status bar or notch padding into the design: mark the region with data-region="top-bar" and let the code add the insets.
claims.states: A state is a parameter, not a separate frame: show every state you want compiled, and reach no state through hover alone, because a touch target has none.
claims.text-overflow: Text that can run long needs a declared line limit: give the maximum line count for every text block that can overflow.
claims.units: Write every length as an absolute px number and nothing else: no em, rem or percent for a layout size, because a relative size has no one meaning across these targets.

targets.block:
- Layout is stacks and grids: VStack, HStack, ZStack, LazyVStack, LazyVGrid and Grid. There is no CSS Grid and no box model, so a gap is padding or spacing and never a margin.
- Text carries a text style rather than a fixed point size, so any string can grow with the user's setting: let containers wrap instead of clip.
- A color, a font or a shape this design does not name has no name in the code, so name it in the brief.
- The code this design becomes has not been written for this target yet: treat every rule here as a limit to design around, not as a promise about an API.

contractHeading: CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS. Every line below is checked on what you export, and a miss is a failure reported back to you.
adviceHeading: DESIGN FOR CONVERTIBILITY. Not contract requirements: these cost nothing and make the generated code better.
advice:
- Ask for one component and its states, not one frame per state. A state is a parameter.
- Show the empty, loading and error variants. A design that skips them becomes code that crashes on the first empty list.
- Use the longest realistic string, not the prettiest one. Truncation is a design decision and it is cheapest while designing.
- Give two width classes or more for anything that will run in a resizable window.
- Say in the brief which decisions you made that a reader cannot see in the markup.
decisionsHeading: DECISIONS FILE. Emit this machine-readable file next to the frames, not only prose.
decisionsBody: The converter reads it instead of guessing, so a component's props arrive as input rather than as a guess about which text varies. When it disagrees with the markup, the markup wins and the disagreement is reported: markup is what was looked at, this file is what was claimed.

podcast-card.notes: cover is a placeholder drawn from a container color, no artwork

invented: card min height 200px, not in the spec
open: does the now playing bar overlay the list or push it?

topicOrderHow: Order is a reading order for a human and a design tool, so it is declared and never derived from a sort. Every topic a prompt-participating row carries must appear here; a topic missing from this list is a usage error (exit 2), which is what stops a new row from silently vanishing from the document.
